newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea grades up a touch, Dtd Brent back to bottom.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea grades up a touch, Dtd Brent back to bottom.

text.p: Most North Sea crude grades were able to command slightly higher premiums on Thursday but benchmark Dated Brent lost ground again.
Intermonth Brent spreads were up about 5-10 cents a barrel in an outright market where Oct Brent jumped 45 cents to $20.70 a barrel.

Dated Brent slipped back to trade again at its recent low of Sept paper -25 cents for a Sept 12-14 loader, probably reflecting buyers' reluctance to pay higher values against October. Sept/Oct Brent was out about 10 cents at +50 cents.
Two of three Brent cargoes nominated loading dates on Thursday were kept, one by BP and one by Elf. BP also was left holding another cargo at the five o'clock deadline.
Oseberg, Forties and Ekofisk all traded on Thursday at the top end of recent ranges at Dated Brent +15 cents, +28 cents and +15 cents respectively.
Two more Osebergs found homes but details remained undisclosed.
Traders said differentials were helped by improving margins, led by gas oil, and a rundown in the North Sea overhang which sliced into premiums last week.
In the Mediterranean, prompt prices for Urals crude remained depressed with most requirements covered for first decade September and 3-4 cargoes loading before September 15.
"Up to the 10th (September) it still looks very weak, but there is some demand beginning to emerge beyond the 10th," a trader with a major refiner said.

Two very prompt cargoes traded Wednesday at around dated Brent -$1.10 a tonne, but the market was now assessed slightly above this level with second decade barrels talked dated Brent -90/-85 cents a barrel.
